variableReadSpelling: VARIABLE-READ SPELLING (php, 2026-10-11). The `uses` targets in this file that name a `$variable` are BINDINGS, not declaration names: the analyzer spells a variable read as `<read source>\u0000<binding>` with `metadata.localBinding`, because a local/param/superglobal is never a published symbol and the BARE name let the store bind the read to an unrelated same-named declaration in another file. The defect and its counterfactual are in validation/m14/fixtures/php/local-read-phantom.mts; the whole-population effect is in docs/analyzers/history/php-lane-notes.md. What each row PINS (which read, from where, and how many) did not move.
rationale: M60 php lane — STATIC vs DYNAMIC member names. A property read names a member only when the name is a static `name` node; the old rule on BOTH sides was a proxy (the analyzer skipped a name whose text starts with `$`, the oracle pushed the raw name-field text), and the proxy is what the dynamic spellings break. Measured with script/m14/tmp/php-dynamic-member-shapes.ts before either side was touched: `$postParams->$param` (phpmyadmin src/Http/ServerRequest.php:233 — the lane's MISSING) had the analyzer emitting NOTHING while the oracle published `uses -> $param`; `$box->{'quoted'}` and `$box->{1}` published a STRING and an INTEGER LITERAL as symbol names, IDENTICALLY on both sides — invisible to the mirror by construction, which is why a fixture independent of the mirror is the only thing that can hold them. The discriminator is the anonymous `{` token the pinned grammar keeps around the name field, probe-verified: `$o->NAME` is [variable_name, ~->, name], `$o->{NAME}` is [variable_name, ~->, ~{, name, ~}]. A braced field is a dynamic selection — no member symbol exists for it in the static graph — and the field's own expression reads come from the ordinary rules (a `$var` through the frame chain, a file const, an inner `$this->x`), which is why `FIELD` and the inner `plain` ARE expected below.
